title: Validity of the deterministic boundary tag
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $p$ be an input-head position among $0,\ldots,n+1$. The tag that is false exactly when $p=0$ and true otherwise is false at the left boundary and true at the right boundary; hence it is a valid boundary tag, with either value allowed at interior positions.
replaced: For every input position, the deterministic nonzero-position tag correctly identifies both boundary blanks and is a valid virtual-input tag for that position.
